newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end firm but off highs, HSBC sheds gains.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end firm but off highs, HSBC sheds gains.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks ended firm on Wednesday but off the day's highs as the Hang Seng Index bumped against resistance and another record-setting rally by HSBC Holdings lost steam.
The Hang Seng Index rose 21.57 points, or 0.16 percent, to 13,541.83 after rising to a high of 13,610.43. Turnover was HK$10.25 billion compared with HK$9.69 billion on Tuesday.

"In general, market sentiment has improved over the last few trading sessions," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities. "But it is really just one or two stocks that have had a very strong performance."
HSBC rallied to a record high of HK$195.50 before closing steady at HK$193.50. Hang Seng Bank fell HK$0.25 to close at HK$91.50 after rising to a high of HK$92.50.
Both are due to release 1996 results on Monday.
Alex Wong, technical analyst at Dharmala Securities, said the Hang Seng seemed to have hit a short-term top at 13,600 and he expected a technical correction over the next couple of days.
"We made a top at 13,600 and then retreated from there."
Wong said investors were also cautious ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to the Senate Banking Committee due later on Wednesday.
"The U.S. long bond looks quite soft to me," he added. "I am expecting the bond yield to rise a little bit so probably that will drive the index down a little bit."
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond ended unchanged on Tuesday to yield 6.66 percent.

But analysts said that over the next month they expected the Hang Seng Index to move higher, with results announcements from Hong Kong's major blue-chip companies and property development sales boosting prices.
"I think these will boost the market next month and we will probably see a re-test of 14,000 points," said Wong.

Hopewell Holdings shares were actively traded on Wednesday. The stock rose HK$0.225 to HK$4.725. Brokers said the stock had been a laggard and they expected covered warrants to be issued on the shares.
Some China-related shares continued to perform well. China Resources advanced HK$1.35 to HK$18.30 and China Eastern Airlines rose HK$0.13 to HK$1.71.
February Hang Seng Index futures gained 20 points to 13,555. The contract expires on Thursday.
